state.seed_assertion: Repair of intermittent faults should be verified under the conditions that previously correlated with failure, monitoring long enough to cover the original occurrence interval.

sentences.1: Repair of intermittent faults should be verified under the conditions that previously correlated with failure, monitoring long enough to cover the original occurrence interval.
sentences.2: Verify the repair under the conditions that previously correlated with failure.
sentences.3: Monitor long enough to cover the original occurrence interval.
sentences.4: Condition monitoring through continuous alarm and signal analysis gives your maintenance team an earlier view into PLC health, so repairs can be scheduled before a failure forces the issue.
sentences.5: Preventive maintenance, corrective repair, inspection, calibration, warranty, and recall may be enough.
sentences.6: The most effective maintenance teams maintain consistency long enough for records to become operationally useful.
sentences.7: They're the ones that stay consistent long enough for the record to become useful.
sentences.8: Software faults tend to be repeatable and occur when a specific set of conditions is present, whereas hardware faults are affected by environmental conditions.
sentences.9: a useful log should capture the basics of the job, the condition of the asset, and enough follow-up detail to support warranty history, planning, and trend review over time.
sentences.10: Digital drives with built-in oscilloscope tools and triggering capability can capture key data prior to the next fault occurrence for analysis.
sentences.11: Measuring voltage at the source and return path is part of systematic troubleshooting to determine circuit condition.
sentences.12: An effective maintenance log must include identification details, job specifics, condition assessments, parts information, technician identification, and follow-up actions.
